Confusable pairs among the point thresholds, suspension periods and restoration rules, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in trailing lines.

FACT_ID: sec05-R01 | anchor: A01
Seven points can send you to a driver improvement clinic, while 12 points within three years can cost you the license; after reinstatement only eight points within three years can bring a second suspension. [A01]
Why it matters: group thresholds; difficulty high; confusable seven, eight and twelve.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R02 | anchor: A01
Completing the clinic removes three points, whereas reinstatement after a suspension cancels every earlier license point. [A01]
Why it matters: group point removal; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R03 | anchor: A01
Reinstating your driving privilege cancels every prior driver license point, though insurance points are not canceled by that reinstatement [A01].
Why it matters: group point systems; confusable license versus insurance points.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R04 | anchor: A01
The adult point-system ladder runs 60 days, then six months, then 12 months for the first, second and third suspension. [A01]
Why it matters: group suspension lengths; confusable with the provisional ladder.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0036]

FACT_ID: sec05-R05 | anchor: A06
For a provisional licensee the ladder runs 30 days, 90 days and six months, counted from the second, third and fourth moving violation within 12 months. [A06]
Why it matters: group suspension lengths; prereq graduated licensing; confusable with the adult point ladder.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]

FACT_ID: sec05-R06 | anchor: A02
On the commercial schedule, passing a stopped school bus carries 8 points and a rail-highway crossing violation 6, yet littering with a vehicle still carries only 1 point. [A02]
Why it matters: group point values; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0037]

FACT_ID: sec05-R07 | anchor: A03
Speeding more than 15 mph over the limit above 55 mph means at least 30 days, but a second such charge within a year, or speeding plus reckless driving on one occasion, means 60 days. [A03]
Why it matters: group speeding revocations; difficulty high.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0038]

FACT_ID: sec05-R08 | anchor: A04
Manslaughter brings a one-year suspension, while manslaughter under the influence of an impairing substance brings a permanent one. [A04]
Why it matters: group offense table; confusable one year versus permanent.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R09 | anchor: A04
Prearranged racing and helping with it carry three years, three times the one-year period for most other offenses in the same table. [A04]
Why it matters: group offense table; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R10 | anchor: A04
A revoked driver first asks DMV for a hearing; only if that fails is the appeal taken to the county Superior Court within 30 days. [A04]
Why it matters: group challenge routes; confusable hearing versus appeal.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0039]

FACT_ID: sec05-R11 | anchor: A05
A driver who cannot pay files a Motion for Relief and asks the judge for relief, while a driver who can pay calls the clerk and pays everything; in both routes the court notifies DMV. [A05]
Why it matters: group unpaid fines; confusable Option A versus Option B.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0040]

FACT_ID: sec05-R12 | anchor: A06
The ordinary restoration fee is $83.50 and the DWI restoration fee is $167.25, while the separate $50 service fee is skipped if the license was surrendered or mailed in before the effective date. [A06]
Why it matters: group fees; dynamic; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0041]
